## a7d4df2828a0

**Reproduced teaching defect: random branch coverage does not identify the control
mapping within a four-demonstration lesson.** Generator SHA-256
`2a710e880d69b1c86cdc64eea19c274c9dd7a26dbcf4bcc06f461c04c8ffca9c`,
rule hash `089b88c1e5ad`.

Exact counterexample: medium difficulty, seed 0, demonstration sample indices
3–6 and query index 7. Their control codes are `[1, 3, 3, 1] -> 2`. The fixed rival
rule uses the intended mappings for codes 1, 3, and 4, but treats code 2 as identity.
It therefore reproduces all four authoritative demonstration outputs and disagrees
on the query, whose code-2 motif is guaranteed to change under the intended 180°
rotation. All five inputs pass `self_check`.

I executed the unchanged Racket authority with the supported `arcpuzzles apply`
command. `checks/audit/a7d4df2828a0/racket.json` records the rule/generator hashes,
inputs, outputs, command, and working directory; `rival.json` records the rival
outputs and confirms `[true, true, true, true, false]` agreement across the four
demos plus query. `input.json`, `metadata.json`, and `apply.log` retain the exact
reproducer.

A broader finite census over 2,000 medium lessons (seeds 0–99, starts 0–19, same
four-consecutive-demo/next-query assembly) found only 211/2,000 demo sets covering
all four control codes, and 663/2,000 queries whose code was absent from every
demonstration. Evidence: `checks/audit/a7d4df2828a0/frequency.json`. A scheduled
four-code teaching profile or executable permutation rivals plus lesson-level
identifiability would address this; I did not modify the audit target.

## a7d4df2828a0

**A2 — reproduced teaching ambiguity even with complete code coverage.**
Generator 2.1.0, SHA-256
`2a710e880d69b1c86cdc64eea19c274c9dd7a26dbcf4bcc06f461c04c8ffca9c`.
Executed rule hash `089b88c1e5ad`; raw rule SHA-256
`fade8c1b99180c908ba1607ad9ce73879331f59b2d23d8e67c3a3892b5a138d5`.

Use medium seed 4. Demonstrations at indices 8, 9, 10, 11 have control codes
`[1,4,2,3]`; query index 12 has code 3. All five inputs are ordinary generated
inputs and pass self_check. Define one fixed rival: retain the intended meanings
of codes 1, 2 and 4, but map code 3 to a vertical reflection rather than a
horizontal reflection. With the five actual Racket labels, agreement is
`[true,true,true,true,false]`. Every control was demonstrated, but the symmetric
code-3 example did not distinguish the meanings needed by the query.

The rival may assign the same operation to two codes; it does not assume that
the legend must be a bijection. This is a plausible fixed color-to-operation
alternative, not a post-hoc per-example rule. The actual and rival query grids,
source/rule hashes and exact code sequence are in
`checks/audit/a7d4df2828a0/verified_witness.json`. The five inputs, actual Racket
labels and all rival predictions are also retained in that directory.

Prior lead `review-227a1cee0f0c5d2a:v0001`, retained archive SHA-256
`64e2e6188e30e50d1f42ae02661be696b0a33c1e7b741b0fe9041db5707b5ac6`,
reported a query control absent from the demos. I used that as a lead, then reproduced the stronger all-codes-present
case above on the pinned source. The earlier pending audit was not silently
resolved by these checks.

A broader diagnostic looked at medium seeds 0–199 and starts 0–9: 2,000
overlapping four-demo/one-query windows. Of 203 windows containing all four demo
codes, 30 still admitted one of three tested single-code alternatives
(1→counterclockwise, 3→vertical reflection, 4→horizontal reflection).
Those frequency counts use a **Python mirror only**. Only the first witness's
five labels were separately Racket-replayed; do not treat the 2,000-window count
as 2,000 independent or authoritative reference executions.

**Suggested task-owner action:** schedule asymmetry witnesses for each control,
or resample complete lessons when a declared operation-family gate finds two
consistent meanings with different query predictions. Counting demonstrated
codes is insufficient. Audit only; no repair included for this task.
